# `render/mesh/SkeletalAnimation.js`

> **Source:** `engine/render/mesh/SkeletalAnimation.js`

============================================================================ SkeletalAnimation.js - CPU skeletal animation + skinning for imported models  Evaluates glTF animations per-frame, computes joint world matrices, and skins vertex positions/normals/tangents on CPU. Updates the GPU vertex buffer via EntityMeshRenderer. ============================================================================

## Functions

### `registerSkinnedMesh(meshKey, geo, skeleton, animations)`

Register a skinned mesh for animation playback.

**Parameters:**

- `meshKey` *(string)* — e.g. 'custom_<uuid>'
- `geo` *(Object)* — { positions, normals, tangents, uvs, indices, joints, weights }
- `skeleton` *(Object)* — { joints[], inverseBindMatrices, jointCount }
- `animations` *(Object[])* — Array of { name, channels[], duration }

Unregister a skinned mesh.

### `getAnimatedBoneShapes(meshKey, entityPos)`

Get ANIMATED bone shapes for visual overlay rendering. Returns current-frame bone positions/rotations with mesh-measured capsule sizes. Uses the CURRENT animated worldMatrices so capsules track the animation exactly. This is the PRIMARY API for the visual bone overlay in Viewport.js. Each bone returns: - pos: world position (midpoint between bone and first child) - rot: quaternion aligning Y-axis with bone direction - radius: mesh-measured perpendicular distance (90th percentile) - halfHeight: half the bone length minus radius - name: bone name for debug/classification - parentIndex: parent bone index (-1 for roots) - isTerminal: true for end/nub bones (skip rendering)

**Parameters:**

- `meshKey` *(string)* — e.g. 'custom_<uuid>'
- `entityPos` *(number[])* — [x,y,z] entity world position

**Returns:** { shapes: [...], bodyHeight, shoulderWidth }

### `getBindPoseBones(meshKey, entityPos)`

Get bind-pose bone data WITHOUT modifying state (no ragdoll, no animation stop). Used for edit-mode SDF collider visualization preview.

**Parameters:**

- `meshKey` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `entityPos` *(number[])* — [x,y,z] entity world position

**Returns:** { bones: [{index, parentIndex, worldPos, worldRot, childPositions, name}], jointCount, rootScale }

### `enableRagdoll(meshKey, entityPos)`

Enable ragdoll mode for a skinned mesh. Stops animation and returns bind-pose bone world positions + hierarchy for creating physics bodies.

**Parameters:**

- `meshKey` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `entityPos` *(number[])* — [x,y,z] entity world position

**Returns:** { bones: [{index, parentIndex, worldPos, childPositions, name}], jointCount }

### `setRagdollBoneTransforms(meshKey, boneWorldMatrices)`

Update bone world matrices from ragdoll physics transforms, then reskin.

**Parameters:**

- `meshKey` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `boneWorldMatrices` *(Float32Array)* — jointCount * 16 column-major matrices

### `disableRagdoll(meshKey)`

Disable ragdoll mode, resuming animation.

## Notes & Examples

### Shared GPU device

Engine subsystems should reuse the cached `GpuDevice` wrapper returned by `getGpuDevice()`. The wrapper owns the native `GPUDevice`, its queue, granted features, limits, and device-loss callbacks. Resources created by one native device cannot be used by another, so pass the shared wrapper or native device into each subsystem that needs GPU access.

**Example: Acquire the shared engine device**
```js
import { getGpuDevice } from '/engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js';

const gpu = await getGpuDevice({
  label: 'MyEngineApp',
  adapterOptions: { powerPreference: 'high-performance' },
  requiredFeatures: []
});

const device = gpu.getDevice();
const queue = gpu.getQueue();
```

Request a feature only when the application cannot run without it. `GpuDevice.create()` automatically requests the engine's supported optional feature set, while `gpu.getCapabilities().features` reports the features actually granted to the device.

**Feature and limit checks**
```js
const { features, limits } = gpu.getCapabilities();

if (features.has('timestamp-query')) {
  console.info('GPU timestamp queries are available');
}

const requestedBytes = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
if (requestedBytes > limits.maxBufferSize) {
  throw new RangeError('Requested buffer exceeds maxBufferSize');
}
```

**Device loss**
```js
gpu.onDeviceLost((info) => {
  console.error('WebGPU device lost:', info.reason, info.message);
  // Stop work and re-bootstrap the application so every GPU resource is rebuilt.
});
```

**Gotchas:**
- **First acquisition defines requirements:** `getGpuDevice()` caches the wrapper. Supply mandatory features and limits on the first call.
- **Native access:** use `gpu.getDevice()` and `gpu.getQueue()` when a subsystem needs WebGPU primitives.
- **Recovery:** this module reports device loss but does not expose an in-place `recreate()` API. Re-bootstrap all device-owned resources together.
- **Limits:** check the granted `gpu.getCapabilities().limits` before large allocations.

(Source: `engine/core/gpu/GpuDevice.js`)
